name: JobsNL Wage Subsidy
provider: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, Department of Jobs, Growth and Rural Development

summary.quote: The JobsNL Wage Subsidy program helps connect employers with employees by providing funding to create long-term or seasonal/short-term jobs.

sources.title: JobsNL Wage Subsidy - Jobs, Growth and Rural Development
sources.terms_note: The province owns the copyright and grants the public permission to use the information on its website; third-party graphics, audio and video may not be reproduced.

funding_types.quote: JobsNL-42: Provides a wage subsidy for 28 weeks within a 42-week employment period.

cost_share.text: 60% to 80% of wages depending on the option and period, up to $12 an hour
cost_share.quote: First 14 weeks: 60% subsidy, up to $12/hour. Second 14 weeks: No subsidy. Third 14 weeks: 80% subsidy, up to $12/hour.

criteria.text: The employer has an office in Newfoundland and Labrador
criteria.quote: Must have an office in Newfoundland and Labrador.

criteria.text: A private or not-for-profit employer that is incorporated or a sole proprietorship
criteria.quote: Private or not-for-profit sector employers that are incorporated or sole proprietorships.

criteria.text: The money helps create a new position
criteria.quote: It offsets salary costs to help create new positions, especially for individuals who lack work experience and skills.

criteria.text: Has a CRA business number and is in good standing with the Registry of Companies and Deeds
criteria.quote: Must have a CRA business number and be in good standing with the Registry of Companies and Deeds.

criteria.text: The person hired lives in Newfoundland and Labrador
criteria.quote: Must reside in Newfoundland and Labrador.

criteria.text: The person hired is unemployed or underemployed
criteria.quote: Must be unemployed or underemployed (working less than 20 hours per week or in a field unrelated to their training).

criteria.text: The person hired is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident in Newfoundland and Labrador
criteria.quote: Must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

criteria.text: The person hired isn’t receiving federal or provincial pensions, Workplace NL benefits or other benefits
criteria.quote: Must not be receiving federal or provincial pensions, Workplace NL benefits, or other benefits.

criteria.text: The person isn't hired before you apply
criteria.quote: Individuals hired before the application date are not eligible.

contacts.label: Employment programs
contacts.quote: Need more Information? Email: EmploymentPrograms@gov.nl.ca Call: 1-800-563-6600

research.notes: Intake: the page never says when applications are taken, so unknown. The subsidy is per hour ('up to $12/hour') with no total maximum on the page, so max_amount is null; cost_share uses the highest rate on the page (80%, the third 14 weeks of JobsNL-42; JobsNL-28 is 60%) and the text says so. Structure: 'Private or not-for-profit sector employers that are incorporated or sole proprietorships' gives corporation and sole_proprietor; a co-operative or non-profit may or may not be incorporated, so those two are unclear (DECISIONS #18). 'Partnership' and 'Not registered yet' are missed. Purpose 'hire' comes from 'help create new positions'. The page also excludes government departments, crown agencies, municipalities and political parties; that doesn't map to our profile and wasn't added. Each participant rule is its own check-this-yourself item with its own quote (gm2 J2): lives in NL, unemployed or underemployed, citizen or permanent resident, not receiving pensions or benefits. Two widening lines stay in these notes: temporary residents may qualify with a Post-graduate Work Permit or an Open Work Permit, and recent post-secondary graduates who haven't found work in their field. The Program Guidelines are linked from the page but were not fetched (PDF). The LaMPSS password help line (1-844-252-6777) is technical support, not a program contact, so it's left out.
